core_obligations: Base change a free resolution of M over R to the second ring, note that exactness may fail, and complete it to a free resolution by adding a further free module (proof lines 24107-24115).
Identify the two complexes computing the relevant Tor groups after dividing by the extended ideal (proof lines 24116-24122).
Write down the vertical map of complexes between them and observe that it induces a surjection on cohomology, which is the claim (proof lines 24122-24134).
proof_roadmap: Complete the base-changed resolution by an extra free module (proof lines 24106-24115).
Compare the two complexes modulo the extended ideal and read off the surjection (proof lines 24116-24135).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map R to R', an ideal I with extension I', and an R-module M, the natural comparison map from Tor_1 over R of the quotient by I' to Tor_1 over R' of the base change is surjective (statement lines 24097-24104). The proof does not compute either Tor group with an explicit resolution over the target ring: it notes that the base change of a free resolution need not remain exact, completes it by an extra free module, identifies the two complexes computing the Tor groups modulo the extended ideal, and exhibits a vertical map of complexes that is visibly surjective on cohomology (proof lines 24106-24135, with the diagram drawn in Xy-pic). Supplying the extra free module so that the comparison becomes a map of complexes is the content, and the author writes the diagram out. H2.
